body:
## Summary

Research for #599, following the maintainer's approved three-case investigation:

- Existing Pydantic decimal/integer constraints and a TDD millisecond-datetime rejection policy.
- A TDD, deliberately narrow final Decimal/text parameter check showing the custom-serializer gap.
- SQLite decimal TEXT/integer-minor-unit recipes and their comparison/storage limits.
- Source audit of existing snekql decimal/temporal fit protections, which must not be accidentally removed in a Pydantic-owned redesign.

Report: `research/precision_loss_599/README.md`.

No public API selected, production/dependency changes, backend suites, native database execution or migrations. Column helper discussion remains a recipe recommendation, not an implemented helper. Final checks are callable experiments, not integrated write hooks. Documentation-derived database facts are separated from executed Python evidence.

## Validation

- `uv run snektest research/precision_loss_599`: 30 passed.
- `uv run ty check`: passed.
- `uv run ruff check .`: passed.
- `uv run ruff format --check .`: passed.
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed before commit.

Existing backend/runtime suites were intentionally not run for this isolated research. No lossless-storage guarantee is inferred from these probes.
title: Research explicit precision-loss protection (#599)
